name: Sprocket
text: Add a "safe change" auto-apply layer that runs after PR-Agent but before human review. It handles only formatting and dependency bumps—no logic changes—so we cut noise without risking bad merges. The trade-off is missing edge cases where formatting or deps could subtly break something, but those are rare and caught by tests. This keeps PR-Agent focused on real issues while speeding up trivial fixes.

name: Gauge
text: The "safe change" layer conflates formatting with dependency bumps—both are mechanical but their risks aren’t uniform. A dependency bump could silently break a build if the new version has breaking changes, while formatting rarely does. Settle it by splitting the layer: auto-apply *only* formatting, and require human review for dependency bumps.

name: Sprocket
text:
Split the safe-change layer into two: auto-apply formatting only, leave dependency bumps for human review. Formatting is zero-risk; deps carry hidden breakage risk. This keeps the noise-cutting benefit for the 99% case while avoiding silent build failures. The trade-off is one extra click for dependency bumps, but that’s cheaper than a rollback.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: Splitting risks conflates *formatting* with *dependency bumps*—a bump could silently break a build if the new version has breaking changes, while formatting rarely does. The real risk isn’t the split—it’s that dependency bumps often *require* human review *only when* the bump crosses a semantic version boundary (major versions). Settle it by auto-applying *only* formatting, but *flag* dependency bumps for human review *only if* the version change is major—otherwise auto-apply minor/patch bumps.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Auto-apply formatting tweaks immediately; route dependency bumps to human review—formatting is zero-risk, deps carry hidden breakage.

Result: PR-Agent + formatting auto-apply layer live; dependency bumps gated behind human review. Owned by Sprocket.
